Questionnaire answers with one row per participant

Source: R/questionnaires.R
gorilla_wide.Rd

Turns the questionnaire answers of read_gorilla() into a wide table with one row per participant and one column per item. Items with a quantised value, such as the position of the chosen option in a dropdown or a Likert scale, get a second column ending in _quantised.

Usage

gorilla_wide(x, task = NULL, quantised = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A gorilla_data object from read_gorilla().

task

Names of the questionnaires to include, as in the task_name column. All by default.

quantised

Add the _quantised columns.

Value

A tibble with participant_private_id and one column per item. Column names are converted to snake case.

Details

Questionnaires from Questionnaire Builder 1 and 2, downloaded in long or short format, give the same columns. An item that appears in more than one questionnaire gets the questionnaire name as a prefix. Objects of Questionnaire Builder 2 that share a name within a questionnaire, such as several objects left with the default name Rating Scale, are different questions and get their object ID as a suffix, as in rating_scale_object_29. If a participant answered the same item more than once, for example after repeating a node or going back to a page, the later answers go into columns ending in __2, __3 and so on. Cleaned item names never contain a double underscore, so these columns cannot be confused with items whose names end in a number.

Examples

g <- read_gorilla(gorilla_example())
#> Skipped 1 file without data (nodes no participant reached): data_exp_123456-v3_questionnaire-zz1e.csv
gorilla_wide(g)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 14
#>   participant_private_id   age gender gender_quantised languages_english
#>   <chr>                  <int> <chr>             <dbl>             <int>
#> 1 9100037                   23 Female                1                 1
#> 2 9100074                   34 Female                1                 1
#> 3 9100111                   22 Female                1                 1
#> 4 9100148                   26 Male                  2                 1
#> 5 9100185                   29 Female                1                 0
#> 6 9100222                   34 Male                  2                 0
#> # ℹ 9 more variables: languages_german <int>, languages_italian <int>,
#> #   languages_portuguese <int>, handedness <chr>, handedness_quantised <dbl>,
#> #   consent_data <chr>, consent_data_quantised <dbl>, consent_withdraw <chr>,
#> #   consent_withdraw_quantised <dbl>
